c1.note: Salesforce's Sept 3, 2026 release announces Core, Advanced and Max editions bundling Slack, Tableau Next, Premier Success Plan and security. Industry pricing was said to follow later, but the editions were introduced as stated.

c2.note: The new editions replace Enterprise, Unlimited and Agentforce 1, per Salesforce's comparisons to those legacy editions and the secondary source. Legacy customers keep their existing pricing.

c4.note: Core Editions are $195 per user/month per Salesforce.

c5.note: Salesforce says Core offers 70% more value than the legacy Enterprise Edition. This is a vendor marketing claim.

c6.note: Advanced Editions are $395 per user/month per Salesforce.

c7.note: Max is $550 per user/month with zero pricing change from Agentforce 1; the pricing page also shows 'from $550'.

c8.note: The release says Max offers nearly 60% more value than Agentforce 1 (the subhead rounds to 60%). This is a vendor claim.

c9.note: Core includes 500,000 Flex Credits; the secondary source states per org per year.

c10.note: Advanced includes 1 million Flex Credits; the per-year basis is from the secondary source.

c11.note: Max includes 2.75M Flex Credits per org per year per the pricing page, which raised it from 2.5M in early October.

c12.note: Existing Agentforce 1 customers can upgrade to Max at no extra cost.

c13.note: The no-cost upgrade comes with up to $500 in added value.

c14.note: The release states existing customer pricing on legacy editions remains unchanged.

c15.note: Industry Edition pricing goes into effect 'later this fall' with no exact date. Status as of Nov 10 is unconfirmed and may already have changed.

c16.note: Salesforce editions announcement says Help Agent with outcome-based pricing is included in Advanced and Max Editions.

c18.note: Negative feedback or a request for human escalation means no charge, per Salesforce's announcement as quoted.

c19.note: Announcement states Data 360 and Agentforce are unmetered during the agent interaction.

c20.note: Announcement states pay-per-resolution pricing is available July '26; later pages show it in the add-ons price list.

c21.note: Salesforce's Service add-ons page lists Help Agent Resolutions at $2 per resolution.

c23.note: Flex Credits are $500 per 100k on the pricing page and in the May 2025 release; the price is current but not a 2026 change.

c24.note: The pricing FAQ still lists Conversation pricing, and Aquiva confirms $2 per conversation as an option; this is a legacy model, not new in 2026.

c25.note: The May 15, 2025 release documents $500 per 100k Flex Credits; the $2 per conversation model predates it, as Aquiva notes.

c26.note: The May 2025 release states one action consumes 20 Flex Credits ($0.10).

c27.note: The pricing page example shows Voice actions at 30 credits and $0.15 each; Aquiva confirms.

c28.note: Aquiva cites a rate card updated April 21, 2026 with rates consistent with 2025; this is a minor detail that does not answer what changed.

c29.note: The pricing page lists the Agentforce User License at $5 per user/month, requiring Flex Credits; this was introduced in 2025.

c30.note: Agentforce for Service is listed at $125/user/month on the add-ons page, a price that has been in place since 2025.

c31.note: Max from $550 is confirmed, but the $150 Industries add-on and the 'Agentforce 1 Editions' name come from an older Aquiva guide; the current page calls it Max, so the combined claim is outdated.

c32.note: The page text says to choose consumption-based pricing (Flex Credits or Conversations) or per-user licensing, and the FAQ confirms both models.

c33.note: The pricing page lists an Agentforce Coworker User License at $50/user/month as a standalone SKU; the per-user SKU is listed as available now and other Coworker features reach GA in November 2026.

c34.note: The Salesforce announcement gives $50 per user per month and lists the per-user SKU as available now; the Nov 4 date is not shown in the passage but is consistent with the November 2026 story.

c35.note: The Availability section lists Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 connectivity, Conversation History, and Skills as available now.

c36.note: Concret.io shows Enterprise at $175 replaced by Core at $195, about 11.4% higher; the Salesforce release confirms the $195 price.

c37.note: Concret.io shows Unlimited at $350 replaced by Advanced at $395, about 12.9% higher; the Salesforce release confirms the $395 price.

c38.note: Concret.io says Starter and Pro Suite are unchanged in price and features; this is a single third-party source.

c39.note: PricingSaaS recorded the rename of Agentforce 1 Editions to Agentforce Max Editions between the Sep 28 and Oct 5 captures.

c40.note: PricingSaaS recorded the Flex Credits limit going from 2.5M to 2.75M per org per year, and the live pricing page shows 2.75M.

c42.note: Concret.io gives 1M credits before the change while PricingSaaS gives 2.5M, so the discrepancy exists; Aquiva also says 1M Flex Credits plus 2.5M Data Cloud credits, suggesting the 2.5M may be a mislabel.

c45.note: The Q2 FY27 release says Agentforce ARR exceeded $1.5B, up over 240% Y/Y, but this is a financial metric rather than a pricing change.

c46.note: Press release states 'Effective Q2 FY27, Agentforce ARR includes our AI offerings, Slackbot and Headless 360'.

c47.note: Coworker per-user SKU, new editions and Help Agent are product-specific additions; pricing page still lists Flex Credits and Conversations alongside per-user.

c48.note: Editions bundle Agentforce with Flex Credits, and consumption/per-user options are offered beyond per-conversation; no direct passage, but consistent with other sources.

c49.note: Disclaimer quoted: pricing and packaging subject to change, availability may vary by region and governed by customer agreements.

c22.note: CIO article says customers can pre-purchase a packet of resolutions, with a minimum of 1,000. This matches both wordings of the claim.

c44.note: Search results for the Q1 FY27 release, including a May 27 Salesforce press release URL, show Agentforce ARR of $1.2B, up 205% year over year. The cited Q2 page only gives the newer figure, over $1.5B up over 240%, so Q1 is superseded. This is an earnings metric, not a pricing change.

c9.note: Salesforce's editions announcement says Core includes 500,000 Flex Credits, Advanced 1 million and Max 2.75 million. The pricing page states 'per org per year' only for Max, so that wording for Core is inferred from the same allowance format.

c29.note: The pricing page lists the Agentforce User License at $5 per user per month and says it requires Flex Credits.

c34.note: The November 4, 2026 Salesforce news post gives Coworker a $50 per user per month price and lists the per-user, per-month SKU under 'Available now'.

c40.note: PricingSaaS recorded the change between Sep 28 and Oct 5, 2026: the Max (formerly Agentforce 1) Flex Credits allowance went from 2.5M to 2.75M per org per year.

c41.note: PricingSaaS logged an Oct 19, 2026 change: 'renames Max Editions card to Max Edition, keeps $550 price'. The live pricing page still shows Max from $550 per user per month.

c47.note: The pricing page still offers Flex Credits, Conversations and per-user licensing. Coworker's $50 per-user SKU, the new editions and Help Agent's $2 per resolution are separate product options added next to those models.
